title: Destructive action without confirmation or recovery
summary: Irreversible or expensive destructive actions need either meaningful confirmation before commitment or a reliable recovery path after it.
problem: A slip can permanently destroy user work when destructive controls behave like ordinary actions.
use_when: Auditing delete, revoke, reset, remove, cancel, or destructive bulk operations
avoid_when: The action is low consequence and fully reversible through a clearly available undo
rationale: Protection should scale with consequence and reversibility.
Not every destructive-looking action needs a modal, but every costly irreversible action needs protection.

signals: irreversible delete occurs on single ambiguous action
bulk destructive action provides neither scope confirmation nor undo
